title: A city of projects
say: Each building is one project built with Claude Code, and each is a real folder on disk. Height is how much work went in: a tower [1] has weeks of sessions, a tent [2] just started. Roof colour says what it needs from me, and the legend [3] decodes it. The app only reads git, Claude's chat logs and one small note file. It never changes anything.

title: It started with one note
say: When a Claude session ends, it writes a short note into the project: what to do next and how I know it works. NEXT ACTION [1] and PROOF [2] are copied straight from `calculator/.claude/session-state.md`. Open in VS Code [3] shows that file. Weeks later the question is: is it still true?

title: What good looks like
say: The gate says PASS [1]. The proof [2] is not just a claim: it is the real output of the unit tests, and the app asked git about the commit it names. Git found it.

title: Break it live
say: Now I change the code but not the note. The command adds a line to `README.md` and commits it, so the note is now older than the code. Watch this building [1] and its gate [2].

title: It noticed
say: STALE [1]. The newest commit, `Live change during the demo`, is seconds old and the note was written before it. So the gate fails [2]: the app stops trusting the note. The fix is what a session does at the end: write a fresh one.

title: Fixed by a fresh note
say: PASS again [1]. `--checkpoint` rewrote the note the way the /coc-checkpoint skill does, and its proof [2] now names the commit made a minute ago, so git can check it again.

title: Stale on its own
say: Nobody touched this one on stage. The next step [1] was written hours before the newest commit, `Streak keeps yesterday when today is unchecked`, so it may already be done. That is what the STALE pill [2] means.

title: A commit that doesn't exist
say: The proof [1] says the tests passed in commit `4f9e2a1`. The app asked git, and that commit was never made. The gate [2] asks the one question that settles it. No AI needed to catch it.

title: A quote that doesn't match
say: Why it matters [1] quotes `NOTES.md`: 'two hours a day'. The file really says 'two hours a week'. Quotes are checked word for word, and the gate [2] flags it.

title: 'Continue' is not a next step
say: When a check fails, the gate [1] asks the one question to fix first. Here the next step [2] just says 'continue', and the blocker `rate limiting is still undecided` names nobody.

title: Waiting on me
say: A blocker with my name on it, `Me [M]: pick the model provider`, turns the roof clay and shows up as waiting on you, here [1] and in the button at the top [2]. That button is my to-do list every morning.

title: The story, told by Claude
say: How it started and where it is now [1], then every session as a chapter [2]. Claude named each chapter; nobody typed this. It comes straight from Claude's chat logs for this folder.

title: Checked, or only written down
say: Every project, failing ones first. For each: what the app checked, yes or no, and what is only someone's word. [1] counts the checks that hold. Scroll down: pomodoro-timer [2] and invoice-parser [3] each have one 'no'.

title: Take it home
say: End every session with three things: the next step, proof it works, and who owns each blocker. Then check the note against the code before you trust it. Every building opens in VS Code, and `demo.code-workspace` in the demo folder opens them all. Press T to hide this guide for questions.
